newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: U.N. to set up medical centre in Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: U.N. to set up medical centre in Sarajevo.

text.p: The United Nations industrial development agency is to set up a bio-medical engineering centre in the Bosnian capital, Sarajevo, in an aid project financed by Japan, the agency said on Thursday.

UNIDO (the U.N. Industrial Development Organisation) will establish the centre for the repair and maintenance of medical equipment over the next three years at Sarajevo's Kosevo hospital at a cost of nearly one million dollars.
The Vienna-based agency said other hospitals in the region were expected to take part in the project, including several from the Bosnian Serb republic.

Many of Bosnia's hospitals were wrecked or left without proper supplies and equipment during three years of war which ended with the signing of the Dayton peace agreement in 1995. Doctors, nurses and medical staff worked under appalling conditions, often risking their own lives, to treat the thousands injured in fighting between the Moslem-led Bosnian government, Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Croats.

Up to 30 percent of medical equipment was reported to be out of order in Bosnia and new devices sent to the country following the Dayton accord could not be operated by untrained staff, according to UNIDO reports.
The project aims to train medical personnel to use new equipment and how to repair minor faults to expensive devices, and plan for future technological needs for the Balkan country's hospitals.
